description: "Host tests, QEMU tests, and CI"

# Testing strategy

## Three layers

```
┌─────────────────┐
│   Host tests    │  bitmap, fmt, ring buffer, scope, manifest…
│ (zig build test)│  normal std, fast feedback
└────────┬────────┘
         │
┌────────▼────────┐
│   QEMU tests    │  boot → serial output assertions
│ (boot-test/CI)  │  "Full boot OK" → pass
└────────┬────────┘
         │
┌────────▼────────┐
│   GDB + QEMU    │  manual debugging during development
└─────────────────┘
```

Host tests (`tests/host/`, `zig build test`) cover pure logic: PMM, heap core, capabilities, ports, ELF parsing, VFS, scope, manifests, signing, and registries. QEMU tests (`zig build boot-test`) assert the serial log line by line — every phase in the roadmap ends with an expected marker, and CI fails until all of them appear.

## Rules

- Deterministic tests first; fake devices before real hardware.
- A fake device must model real behavior (timeouts, races, bad sequences) — never a mock that accepts everything.
- Never weaken a test to make development convenient; CI failures are data.
- The 1.0 gate workflow stays red until every requirement has evidence — the failing status is intentional: *we are not at 1.0 yet*.

## Debugging a failure

```bash
zig build test          # fast: did pure logic break?
zig build               # does the freestanding kernel still compile?
zig build boot-test     # which serial marker is missing?
```

The first missing marker names the broken phase; the chapter for that phase names the files.
